canonical_name: Hopf observation with a kept fibre (and the Lorentz read)
aliases: S7 quaternionic Hopf relation state (conditional, never implemented)
plain_what: A way of looking at a rotation state, a point on a four-dimensional sphere, through a three-dimensional shadow that forgets one angle, while separately keeping that forgotten angle so nothing is lost. It was used to track drifting phase and to bin states into routing sectors. A related curved-space distance, the Lorentz read, was also tried for scoring.
how_it_works: A unit quaternion q = (a, b, c, d) lies on the 3-sphere S3. The Hopf map sends it to the 2-sphere S2 by h(q) = (2(ac + bd), 2(bc - ad), a^2 + b^2 - c^2 - d^2). Multiplying q by a common complex phase e^(i*phi) moves it along a circle (the fibre) but leaves h(q) unchanged, so the S2 image alone cannot be inverted. Reconstruction needs the S2 base, the S1 fibre phase and a chart convention (poles are special); there is no global identification S3 = S2 x S1. Holonomy tracking accumulates the wrapped fibre-phase change and the Fubini-Study geodesic distance along a state trajectory. Sector routing bins three Hopf coordinates (chi, delta, alpha) into 8 x 8 x 8 = 512 sectors, of which at most 64 are reachable when the inputs are non-negative. The Lorentz read lifts query q and key k to the hyperboloid, q0 = sqrt(1 + |q|^2), k0 likewise, z = q0*k0 - q.k, and scores beta * (delta - arccosh z), with a learned radius delta and a scale beta, as an alternative to a dot product. In the integer runtime the Hopf fibre and zeta state are tracked as telemetry only and do not affect outputs.
geometry: Unit quaternions on S3 (Q30 fixed point), the Hopf fibration S1 -> S3 -> S2, the 120 icosians' Hopf image (30 points, fibres of size 4), Fubini-Study distance on the Bloch sphere, hyperbolic space as the Lorentz hyperboloid, and a conditional S7 -> S4 extension.

status_reason: The map and kept fibre are built and unit-tested but run only as integer-runtime telemetry; the retained-fibre comparison was never run for language (docs/labs/course-correction-2026-10-18/audits/mechanism-census.md). Tested prediction forms failed or used banned parts: sector routing filled 7 of 512 sectors, softmax Lorentz attention, and a Lorentz read neutral or slightly ahead of dot product.
reopen_conditions: Retained-fibre test: base-only vs base plus fibre vs explicit bank tags at equal retained bytes, with fibre removal or permutation, a common action, one endpoint changed vs both, and exact occurrence identity kept outside the lossy summary.
An integer, multiplier-free Hopf map (the current Q30 helpers use integer multiply and divide, or decode to f64 and call sin/cos) wired into a consumer on the discrete path.

A Lorentz or hyperbolic read re-registered as an offline D37 float sheet with a fresh FIT, a read that avoids softmax and dense matmul, a third paired seed, and a D11 export gap (an integer arccosh table does not exist yet).
The reduced finite S7 construction (relative lookup on finite 2I as baseline) only after a witnessed information or cost need.
Hierarchy-heavy tasks where hyperbolic keys already showed a large gap (77.5% vs 0.4% for dot product on code scopes) put on an equal-capacity, softmax-free harness.

rule_compat.D11: Not yet. The integer crate's Hopf helpers are Q30 integer arithmetic but include multiplication and division, and the core helpers decode to f64. The Lorentz read needs arccosh, and the integer runtime refuses Lorentz models until an integer arccosh table exists (cycle 2, section 6). Hopf in the integer runtime is telemetry, not served output.
rule_compat.D23: The Hopf map has no softmax. Every Lorentz read and the HELM-D attention that were actually run normalised scores with softmax (read mass, a NoRead logit), which D23 excludes as executed forms.
rule_compat.D30: The map itself is a few bilinear products, not a matrix multiplication. The float Lorentz stacks use dense learned query and key projections and inner products q.k, which D25/D30 bar.
rule_compat.D32_D37: Float Hopf helpers (sin, cos, sqrt) lie outside the D32 zeta-zero exception. D37 allows offline float training, so a float Hopf or Lorentz read could be re-registered with a fresh FIT, but the discrete Route, Flock and Relation reads currently use no Hopf quantity (docs/geometry.md section 5).

figure_ideas: A rotating 3-sphere picture. Show one unit quaternion as a point on S3 (drawn as its stereographic projection), its S2 shadow as a dot on a sphere next to it, and the fibre as a circle through the point. Drag a phase slider: the S3 point moves around its circle while the S2 dot stays put. A second readout accumulates the winding as 'kept fibre phase', so viewers see exactly what the shadow forgets. (Static art already exists at docs/figures/geometry/hopf-fibration.svg to animate.)

A 512-cell sector grid that lights the cells occupied by the old routing: 7 of 512 with magnitude-only inputs (a tiny corner, the reachable 64 outlined) and 43 of 512 after signed projection. Under it, the retrieval number that did not move (MRR 0.0045 vs 0.0743).

Two readers scoring the same query against stored keys: a flat dot product and a hyperbolic distance on a disk. On a nested tree of code scopes the hyperbolic disk keeps parents near the centre and finds the right ancestor (77.5%), while the flat picture crowds them (0.4%). A second panel shows the same swap in a language model, with the small bars: 0.018 nats, 3 of 4 seeds.
